hints: Focus on structure and bonding first, metals conduct well, silicon conducts a little, and molecular non-metals hardly conduct at all.
Check row 1: sodium is a metal, silicon is a semiconductor metalloid, and chlorine is a molecular insulator, so that order makes sense.
Compare the two metals in row 2 and the two non-metals in row 3 using number of delocalised electrons to decide which row still holds true.
walkthrough:
**Recall the conductivity pattern across Period 3**

Think structure first. Giant metallic on the left, giant covalent in the middle, simple molecular on the right.

Conductivity trend: $\text{metals} > \text{silicon (semiconductor)} > \text{non-metals (insulators)}$

**Compare metals with each other**

Among the metals, conductivity generally increases with more delocalised electrons per atom.

Order: $\text{Al (3 e}^-\text{ per atom)} > \text{Mg (2 e}^-\text{ per atom)} > \text{Na (1 e}^-\text{ per atom)}$

**Test row 1**

Sodium is metallic, silicon is a semiconductor, chlorine is $\text{Cl}_2$ molecules with no mobile charges.

So $\text{sodium} > \text{silicon} > \text{chlorine}$ is correct.

**Test rows 2 and 3 and conclude**

Row 2: aluminium beats magnesium as above, and magnesium (metal) beats phosphorus ($\text{P}_4$ insulator). So $\text{aluminium} > \text{magnesium} > \text{phosphorus}$ is correct.

Row 3: silicon as a semiconductor must beat sulfur, which is an $\text{S}_8$ insulator. So $\text{sulfur} > \text{silicon} > \text{phosphorus}$ is wrong.

Only rows 1 and 2 are correct.

options.A: States rows 1, 2 and 3 are all correct. Rows 1 and 2 are correct, but row 3 is reversed because silicon (semiconductor) conducts better than sulfur (molecular insulator).
options.B: States rows 1 and 2 only are correct. Row 1 follows metals > semiconductors > insulators, and row 2 follows Al > Mg due to more delocalised electrons, with both metals above phosphorus.
options.C: States rows 2 and 3 only are correct. Row 2 is correct, but row 3 is incorrect, so this combination fails. Sulfur and phosphorus are both insulators with essentially zero conductivity, both below silicon.
options.D: States row 1 only is correct. Row 1 is correct, but this misses row 2 which is also correct. Many students doubt Al > Mg, but Al has 3 delocalised electrons per atom and smaller, more highly charged ions, giving higher conductivity.
